messages:
jamie: incident-bot fired a high-severity: apiserver latency + controller-manager restarts in ap-south1 :grimacing:
incident-bot: [ALERT] apiserver_p99_latency > 1200ms for 3m; controller-manager restart_count increased by 8 in last 10m
jamie: noticed etcd WAL growth on nvme0n1, iops saturated. GPUs failing to attach because provisioner API calls time out
alex: can you paste iostat and `kubectl get pods -n kube-system`?
maria: copying logs from node-12 (nvme):
```
# iostat -xz 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s    rkB/s   wkB/s  rrqm/s wrqm/s r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         250.00  180.00  20480.00 40960.00     0.00   0.00   3.12   5.89  0.40  99.70
```
ryan: kube-system pods: `kube-apiserver-node-12` OOM? restarts 3, controller-manager restarted, provisioner pods are `CrashLoopBackOff`
jamie: looks like snapshot compaction stalled; etcd compactor pod logs show repeated ECONNRESET to disk service. suspect underlying host degraded IO after nightly backup window
alex: checklist: 1) scale down compactor frequency? 2) cordon node-12 and migrate provisioner replicas 3) enable provisioning fallback to dedicated-reserved pool in us-central (cost hit)
maria: cordoning now, draining provisioner replicas off node-12 (`kubectl drain node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`) :thumbsup:
ryan: draining blocked by long-running leader-election locks in controller-manager, they're stuck waiting on apiserver watch timeouts
jamie: temporary mitigations: reduce controller-manager leader-election renewDeadline to 10s? risky. alternative: increase apiserver --apiserver-max-connections? ops-doc suggests toggling `--max-requests-inflight` and bump kube-apiserver replicas by 1 for the zone
alex: i've opened a billing-approved change to spin up 4 reserved GPUs in us-central as fallback (cc @finance). ETA 7m to boot + kube join
maria: compactor pod restarted after node cordon, WAL trimming resumed, iops back down to 35% on nvme for node-12 :relieved:
jamie: controller-manager leader-election stabilized, provisioner replicas recovered, new GPU attach requests started succeeding :tada:
ryan: postmortem action items: (1) add persistent iops monitor alert for NVMe > 80% for 2m (2) add automatic quick-fallback to reserved pool when attach_timeout > 15s (3) playbook update for compactor backpressure
jamie: agree. tagging docs/ops and scheduling on-call blameless review tomorrow 10:00 PT
alex: noting cost impact ~+$1.2k for fallback capacity this incident, capture in billing ticket
maria: marking thread resolved. thanks team :eyes:
